extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive procedural requirements for preparing and filing patent drawings, models/exhibits, computer program listings, information disclosure statements (IDS), and for procedural actions such as advancing, suspending, deferring, or examining U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters and lead lines in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters are required for each reference except those indicating the surface or cross section on which they are placed; such a reference character must be underlined to show a lead line has not been omitted. Lead lines must be executed in the same way as lines in the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underline reference characters that sit on a surface or cross section so it is clear no lead line was intended; draw lead lines consistent with drawing line style. See paragraph (l) for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of arrows in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at the ends of lines provided their meaning is clear: (1) on a lead line, a freestanding arrow indicates the entire section towards which it points; (2) on a lead line, an arrow touching a line indicates the surface shown by the line when viewed along the direction of the arrow; (3) arrows may show the direction of movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use arrows only where their intended meaning matches one of the enumerated uses to avoid ambiguity in the drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement and content in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be placed within the sight of the drawing immediately below the figure representing the copyrighted or mask work material and be limited to letters .32 cm to .64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high. Content limited to elements provided by law (e.g., “©1983 John Doe” or “*M* John Doe”). Inclusion permitted only if authorization language of § 1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep notices small, limited to legally sufficient elements, placed immediately below the relevant figure, and ensure the specification includes the authorization language per § 1.71(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, within the sight. If present, numbers must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (or right-hand side if drawing extends too close to middle). Numbers must be clear and larger than reference characters and shown as two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique line: sheet_number/total_number_of_sheets, with no other marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place sheet numbers within the usable drawing sight, centered at top (or right if needed), ensure they are larger than reference numerals, and use the X/Y format to show sheet number and total sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering, and, if possible, in order of appearance on the sheet(s). Partial views forming one complete view must share the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers must be preceded by 'FIG.' except where only a single view is used—in that case it must not be numbered nor include 'FIG.' Numbers/letters identifying views must be simple, clear, not used with brackets/circles/quotes, and must be larger than reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number multi-view drawings as FIG.1, FIG.2, etc., use lettered suffixes (e.g., 3A) for partial/continued views, avoid decorative enclosures, and omit numbering/FIG. text when only a single view is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place any authorized security markings outside the usable drawing area to avoid interfering with reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to drawings must be durable and permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ephemeral corrections (e.g., pencil erasures); submit corrected, permanent media so corrections remain legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should not make holes in drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not punch holes in drawing sheets when submitting; maintain intact sheets compatible with Office handling and reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must meet requirements before examination (§1.85)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility or plant application will not be placed on the files for examination until objections to the drawings have been corrected. Except as provided in § 1.215(c), patent application publication will not include drawings filed after the application has been placed on the files for examination. Objections to drawings will not be held in abeyance unless applicant is notified otherwise, and a request to hold objections in abeyance is not considered a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to drawing objections promptly; do not expect the Office to hold drawing objections open or admit late drawings for publication, unless specific exceptions apply. For design applications, if drawings meet § 1.84(e)-(g) and are suitable for reproduction but not otherwise compliant with § 1.84, they may be admitted for examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not release drawings for correction; submit new corrected drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not release drawings for purposes of correction. If corrections are necessary, new corrected drawings must be submitted within the time set by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect to retrieve drawings for in-hand correction; prepare and file replacement corrected drawings per Office scheduling and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected drawings at allowance: 3-month requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a corrected drawing is required or a drawing does not comply with § 1.84 (or § 1.1026 for international design apps) at time of allowance, the Office may set a three-month period from the notice of allowability within which the applicant must file a corrected drawing to avoid abandonment. This time is not extendable under § 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file corrected drawings within the three-month allowance-period if notified at allowance; do not rely on extension under § 1.136 for these corrected drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of models or exhibits (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model or exhibit will not be admitted as part of the record of an application unless it: (1) substantially conforms to § 1.52 or § 1.84; (2) is specifically required by the Office; or (3) is filed with a petition including the fee under § 1.17(h) and an explanation of why entry of the model/exhibit is necessary to demonstrate patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submit physical models/exhibits if they conform to drawing/spec requirements, are requested by the Office, or accompanied by a successful petition explaining necessity and paying the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require a model or exhibit when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the general rule, the Office may require a model, working model, or other physical exhibit if deemed necessary for any purpose in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared that the Office can compel a model/exhibit if essential to examination—even absent applicant request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs required if a model/exhibit does not conform
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the model or exhibit substantially conforms to § 1.52 or § 1.84, it must be accompanied by photographs that show multiple views of the material features and that substantially conform to § 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting a nonconforming physical exhibit, include compliant photographs showing all material features per drawing standards to permit examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens for compositions of matter may be required
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention relates to a composition of matter, the applicant may be required to furnish specimens of the composition, or of its ingredients or intermediates, for inspection or experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemical/biological compositions, expect possible requests for material specimens to enable examination or testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return and disposal of models, exhibits, specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Models/exhibits/specimens may be returned if no longer necessary; applicant must arrange return at applicant’s expense and the Office may dispose of perishables without notice unless applicant requested return and made prompt arrangements. Applicant is responsible for retaining the actual model/exhibit/specimen for the enforceable life of any resulting patent, except where the item conforms to § 1.52/1.84, is described by photographs conforming to § 1.84, or is perishable. Failure to arrange return within the notice period permits the Office to dispose of the item. Extensions of time are available under § 1.136 except for perishables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want return of submitted physical items, notify the Office on submission and promptly arrange return when notified, or risk disposal; retain originals as needed for enforcement unless permitted exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of exhibits generally not furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of models or other physical exhibits will not ordinarily be furnished by the Office, and any model or exhibit shall not be taken from the Office except in the custody of an employee specially authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect to receive reproductions of physical exhibits from the Office; physical transfer from Office custody is restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listings: descriptive requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of the operation and general content of computer program listings should appear in the description portion of the specification. A computer program listing is a document that lists, in appropriate sequence, the instructions, routines, and other contents of a program and may be submitted in machine or machine-independent (object or source) language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explanatory description in the specification so examiners can understand the program listing’s operation and content rather than relying solely on raw code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formats and placement for computer program listings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the listing is submitted as drawings it must comply with drawing requirements (§ 1.84) and have at least one figure numeral per sheet. If submitted as part of the specification, it must comply with § 1.52. Any listing having more than 60 lines of code submitted as part of the specification must be positioned at the end of the description but before the claims; any amendment must be by substitute sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate submission format: as drawings (follow § 1.84) or part of the spec (follow § 1.52), and place longer listings (>60 lines) at the end of description before claims to facilitate processing and amendments via substitute sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix (electronic) — >300 lines rule and incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any computer program listing may, and any listing having over 300 lines (up to 72 characters per line) must, be submitted as an electronic document in ASCII plain text (a 'Computer Program Listing Appendix') whether submitted via EFS or on a read-only optical disc, in compliance with § 1.52(e). The Appendix will not be part of the printed patent. The specification must include an incorporation by reference of the Appendix per § 1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For listings >300 lines, prepare an ASCII plain text electronic Appendix and ensure the specification includes the required incorporation-by-reference paragraph so the Appendix is properly referenced even though it won’t print in the issued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Program Listing Appendix technical file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Computer Program Listing Appendix must conform to: computer compatibility (PC or Mac), OS compatibility (MS–DOS, MS–Windows, Mac OS, or Unix/Linux), line terminator ASCII CRLF or LF only, and no dependence on control characters outside the ASCII set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce ASCII plain text files that are portable across PC/Mac and use only standard ASCII line endings and characters to avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic file naming, size, compression, and submission rules for listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each file must be named *.txt with a basename up to 60 characters using only upper/lower letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores (no spaces). Each file submitted via EFS must not exceed 25 MB and file compression is not permitted. For read-only optical discs, submit in duplicate labeled 'Copy 1' and 'Copy 2' and include a transmittal letter asserting discs are identical; if not identical, 'Copy 1' will be used. Nested-file-structure listings submitted per § 1.52(e) may be compressed (WinZip/7-Zip/Unix Zip) but compressed files must not be self-extracting, and very-large compressed text files may be split to fit disc sizes and labeled accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow strict naming conventions, respect EFS size limits (25MB) and compression prohibitions for EFS, and if using optical disc media prepare duplicate labeled discs and transmittal letter; compressed archives are allowed only in certain disc submission contexts and cannot be self-extracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and replacement rules for electronic listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendments to an electronic Computer Program Listing Appendix must include a replacement ASCII plain text file submitted via EFS or on read-only optical disc (duplicate) labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY'; include a request for amendment by incorporation by reference in a separate paragraph identifying file name, date, and byte size; include a statement identifying locations of deletions/replacements/additions; and a statement that the replacement ASCII file contains no new matter. If a listing was filed on the application filing date without incorporation by reference, the specification must be amended to contain a separate incorporation-by-reference paragraph per § 1.77(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When replacing or amending electronic listings, submit replacement files with clear labeling and specification paragraphs that identify the replacement and certify no new matter; ensure file metadata (name/date/size) is referenced in the spec amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filing timing windows (§1.97(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement (IDS) will be considered if filed by the applicant within any one of the following: (1) within three months of the filing date of a national application other than a continued prosecution application under § 1.53(d); (2) within three months of entry of the national stage (§ 1.491) in an international application; (3) before mailing of a first Office action on the merits; (4) before the mailing of a first Office action after filing an RCE under § 1.114; or (5) within three months of publication of the international registration under Hague Article 10(3) in an international design application. IDS must satisfy § 1.98 and be accompanied by any applicable IDS size fee under § 1.17(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to file IDS within one of the early windows listed to have it considered without extra statements or fees; ensure compliance with § 1.98 content requirements and pay size fee if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late IDS filing conditions (§1.97(c) and (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after the §1.97(b) period will be considered if filed before mailing of any final action, notice of allowance, or other action closing prosecution and is accompanied by either (1) the statement specified in §1.97(e) or (2) the fee under §1.17(p). An IDS filed after that but on or before payment of the issue fee will be considered if accompanied by the §1.97(e) statement and the fee under §1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing an IDS late, include the required §1.97(e) statement or pay the late fee per §1.17(p) to have the IDS considered; be mindful of final action, allowance, and issue-fee deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required IDS statement content (§1.97(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement must state either: (1) that each item in the IDS was first cited in any communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the IDS; or (2) that no item was cited in such a foreign communication and, to the knowledge of the signer after reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a late IDS pathway, provide the correct certification about the timing and knowledge of cited items to satisfy procedural requirements and enable consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions for IDS filing; allowance for inadvertent omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No extensions of time for filing an IDS are permitted under § 1.136. If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with § 1.98 but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File IDS on time; if an inadvertent omission occurred but you made a bona fide attempt, the Office may allow additional time to correct content though general extensions under §1.136 are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS does not imply a search was made or admission of materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed in accordance with § 1.97 shall not be construed as a representation that a search has been made, nor shall its filing be construed as an admission that the information cited is material to patentability as defined in § 1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an IDS is a disclosure procedure and does not amount to admitting the references are material or that a complete search was performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliant IDS placement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDS does not comply with § 1.97 or § 1.98, it will be placed in the file but will not be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure IDS fully complies with timing, content, and form rules of §§1.97–1.98; otherwise it will be ignored though it may remain in the file record.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS content: required list structure and per-page requirements (§1.98(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDS must include a list of all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted. U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications must be listed separately from other documents. Each page of the list must include: (i) the application number of the application in which the IDS is being submitted; (ii) a column for the examiner’s initials next to each document; and (iii) a heading clearly indicating the list is an information disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format the IDS list carefully to include application number, an examiner-initial column, and a clear heading; separate U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications from other citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS content: required legible copies (§1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a legible copy of: each foreign patent; each publication or the portion that caused listing (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent app publications unless required); for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including claims and any drawing or the portion that caused listing; and all other information or the portion that caused listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include readable copies of cited documents or the specific portions relied upon to permit examiner review; do not assume the Office has the needed copy unless relying on properly identified earlier application per (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS content: non-English documents and translations (§1.98(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the relevance of each non-English patent/publication (as presently understood by the most knowledgeable individual designated in § 1.56(c)) is required. A copy of a translation must be provided if an English translation is in the possession, custody, control of, or is readily available to any individual designated in § 1.56(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-English references, provide a brief relevance statement and a translation if one is readily available to designated individuals; this helps examiners assess the citation without delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS content: fee assertion (§1.98(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear written assertion that the IDS is accompanied by the applicable IDS size fee under § 1.17(v) or a clear written assertion that no such fee is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether an IDS size fee is paid or not required to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS identification requirements for different document types (§1.98(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. patent must be identified by inventor, patent number, and issue date. Each U.S. patent application publication by applicant, publication number, and publication date. Each U.S. application by inventor, application number, and filing date. Each foreign patent/published foreign application by country/office, document number, and publication date. Each publication by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, date, and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete bibliographic identification for each cited document according to its type to enable accurate examiner retrieval and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative disclosures handling in IDS (§1.98(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents/publications listed are substantively cumulative, a copy of one of them may be submitted without copies of the others provided it is stated that the other patents/publications are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple cited items repeat the same disclosure, submit a representative copy and state which other citations are cumulative to reduce redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required even if previously submitted unless properly identified (§1.98(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any cited patent, publication, pending U.S. application, or other information is required, even if previously submitted to the Office, unless (1) the earlier application is properly identified in the IDS and relied on for an earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120; and (2) the IDS submitted in the earlier application complied with §§ 1.98(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume previously-filed copies obviate the need to resubmit — either identify and rely on the earlier application properly or include fresh copies as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement of examination: general rule (§1.102(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be advanced out of turn for examination or further action except as provided by part, upon order of the Director to expedite business, upon filing of a request under paragraphs (b) or (e), or upon filing of a petition or request under (c) or (d) with a showing that justifies advancing it in the Director’s opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect normal queueing unless specific statutory/regulatory exceptions, Director action, or qualifying requests/petitions are filed and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement for public-service importance (§1.102(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications deemed of peculiar importance to some branch of the public service may be advanced for examination if the head of the relevant Government department requests immediate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government requests for inventions of special public importance can move an application ahead of the queue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special on age/health grounds (fee waived) (§1.102(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make an application special may be filed without a fee if the basis is the inventor’s or a joint inventor’s age or health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this fee-waived pathway to expedite prosecution for qualifying inventor circumstances; follow petition requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special on other grounds (fee required) (§1.102(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make an application special on grounds other than age/health must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-age/health special petitions require payment of the applicable fee and appropriate justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination (Track One) requirements and limits (§1.102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination must comply with paragraph (e) and be accompanied by the prioritized examination fee (§ 1.17(c)), the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)), and, if not already paid, the publication fee (§ 1.18(d).) An application for prioritized examination may not contain or be amended to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or any multiple dependent claim. Prioritized examination is not available for international applications not yet national-stage, design, reissue, provisional, or reexamination proceedings. No more than 20,000 requests will be accepted in any fiscal year. Additional procedural and filing conditions apply per (e)(1) and (e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain prioritized examination, pay required fees and ensure claim counts/composition meet strict limits; file deadlines and method (EFS for utility) and one-month cure windows for excess claims apply; monitor annual request cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination filing specifics when filed with original application (§1.102(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request may be filed with an original utility or plant nonprovisional application. The application must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including at least one claim, a drawing when necessary, and the inventor’s oath or declaration on filing (oath/declaration may be postponed if ADS conditions are met). Utility applications must be filed via EFS and include filing, search, and examination fees upon filing; plant applications include corresponding fees. Applicant may file an amendment to cancel any excess independent/total claims or multiple dependent claim not later than one month from a first decision on the prioritized-exam request; this one-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting prioritized examination with the initial filing, ensure the application is complete per 112, pay fees, file via EFS for utility apps, and be ready to timely withdraw excess claims within the non-extendable one-month cure period after the PTO’s first decision on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination filing with/after RCE (§1.102(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination may be filed with or after a request for continued examination (RCE). For utility applications the request must be filed via EFS and before mailing of the first Office action after the RCE filing. Only a single such prioritized-exam request may be granted in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pursuing prioritized examination post-RCE, file via EFS and observe the deadline relative to the first OA after the RCE; only one prioritized grant is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action by the Office on request for good cause (§1.103(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: On applicant request, the Office may grant suspension of action for good and sufficient cause for up to six months. Petitions must specify the period (≤6 months), include a showing of good cause, and include the fee (§ 1.17(g)) unless the cause is the fault of the Office. The Office will not suspend action if a reply to an Office action is outstanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this mechanism to temporarily pause prosecution for justified reasons, include required showing and fee, and avoid requesting suspension when responses to OAs are pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited suspension for continued prosecution applications (CPA) (§1.103(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: On applicant request, the Office may grant suspension of action in a CPA filed under § 1.53(d) for a period not exceeding three months. Requests must be filed with the CPA, specify the period, and include the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs can obtain short suspensions (≤3 months) with proper request and fee filed at CPA submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited suspension after RCE (§1.103(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing an RCE, applicant may request suspension of action for up to three months; the request must be filed with the RCE, specify the period, and include the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine suspension requests with RCE filing when seeking a short delay in prosecution after an RCE, and pay the processing fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination up to three years (§1.103(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: On applicant request, the Office may grant a deferral of examination for up to three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed. Requests must include the publication fee (§ 1.18(d)) and processing fee (§ 1.17(i)). Deferral will not be granted unless: (1) the application is an original utility or plant app filed under § 1.53(b) or resulting from entry of an international app into national stage after compliance with § 1.495; (2) applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under § 1.213(a) (or has rescinded one under § 1.213(b)); (3) application is in condition for publication under § 1.211(c); and (4) the Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral up to 3 years is available if publication-related fees and conditions are met and no OA/allowance has been issued; do not request deferral if you have nonpublication pending or if application is not ready for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated suspension and suspension for public safety/defense (§1.103(e)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will notify applicant if it suspends action on its own initiative. The Office may suspend action by order of the Director if: (1) the application is owned by the United States; (2) publication may be detrimental to public safety or defense; and (3) the appropriate department/agency requests such suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert for Office-initiated suspensions, especially for government-owned applications or national security/public-safety concerns where publication could be harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of examination — examiner duties (§1.104(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application, the examiner must make a thorough study of the application and a thorough investigation of available prior art relating to the claimed invention. Examination shall be complete with respect both to compliance with applicable statutes and rules and to patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as matters of form unless otherwise indicated. The applicant (or patent owner and requester in reexamination) will be notified of the examiner’s action; reasons for adverse action or any objection/requirement will be stated in an Office action with information or references useful to aid the applicant in judging whether to continue prosecution. An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect comprehensive statutory and prior-art analysis by the examiner; Office Actions will state reasons and references to help the applicant assess next steps. International-type searches apply to newer national applications.
